relationship: Semantic port into the canonical McCluster data plane. No upstream bytes are copied; no production data and no seed row is included.

upstream.status: Unpublished review evidence; contains known audit defects. Not an installable release or authorization to apply.

ported_files.notice: -- Portable, private control baseline. Not a production Supabase migration.
-- Additive v1 -> v2 upgrade. Existing settings, owners, policy revisions and idempotency receipts are retained.

license.note: Patches retain original source/license context; redistribution terms are not changed.

ported_semantics: states enabled, draining, disabled; enabled -> disabled refused until drained
revision 0..9007199254740991, incremented only on a real state change; no-ops audited
owner command idempotency: exact replay returns the stored receipt, changed replay fails
guard taken in the domain write's own transaction and held to commit
new modules start disabled; nothing is deleted; runtime holds function grants only and no table privilege
deliberate_differences: installations/owners tables, installer, schema_versions, restricted runtime role and equity.* settings are not ported: public.orgs, public.org_members(role='owner'), the Supabase ledger and service_role are the canonical authorities
provision() is replaced by an owner-authorised install command; the migration creates no row

the guard adds a per-module transaction-level advisory lock (shared) in front of the upstream FOR SHARE row lock, and the owner command takes it exclusively, because a new FOR SHARE locker is admitted ahead of a waiting FOR UPDATE on native PostgreSQL 16.15 and 17.7
refusals carry stable SQLSTATEs EUM00..EUM07 (upstream distinguishes them by message text only)
the expected policy revision on a guarded write is optional (required for jobs, optional for one-request commands)
a non-empty reason (1..500 characters) is required; upstream allowed an empty one
idempotency key is the E=Up text key (8..128 safe characters) instead of a uuid

a reduce-only entry point public.eup_module_guard_reduce(p_module text) exists beside the guard (upstream has one guard and no such door). Reason: actions that only stop work or remove exposure (a member revoking consent and the publication withdrawal it causes, withdrawing an application or assignment, discarding an upload, withdrawing an appeal, an owner pausing or withdrawing a campaign or mission, withdrawing a publication, placing a moderation hold, recording a media purge, revoking an audience grant, pausing an intake source) must stay possible while a module is draining or disabled; refusing them would trap a member's consent or keep retained media past its date. It takes the same shared advisory lock and FOR SHARE row lock as the guard and holds both to commit, so a state command still waits for an in-flight reduce writer; it raises EUM00 and EUM01 only

the statement-trigger backstop public.eup_module_guard_trigger() skips the full guard when the transaction-local marker eup.module_reduce (set only by the reduce-only entry point) names that trigger's own module; a marker for another module, an empty one or none runs the full guard. Reason: a reduce-only action writes the same guarded tables. The marker is a correctness backstop, not a security boundary against the service role
service_role therefore executes six functions, not upstream's five: policy_read, control_read, policy_install, policy_command, guard, guard_reduce
the file is idempotent (create ... if not exists, create or replace) so a second run changes nothing; upstream's baseline is a one-shot installer step
the trigger function returns the row when it is attached FOR EACH ROW by mistake, so a mis-attached backstop still guards instead of silently dropping the write
status: Pending, unapplied, reviewed local schema. Creates no policy row; applying it changes no behaviour until a domain file calls the guards.

stable_codes.EUM00: module_policy_unavailable: the house organisation row is absent or the module id is null
stable_codes.EUM01: module_not_installed: no policy row for the module (read, guard, reduce guard, trigger, state command)
stable_codes.EUM02: module_draining: guarded write refused while draining
stable_codes.EUM03: module_disabled: guarded write refused while disabled
stable_codes.EUM04: module_policy_changed: the expected policy revision passed to the guard differs
stable_codes.EUM05: drain_required: enabled -> disabled refused until drained
stable_codes.EUM06: command_conflict: an idempotency key replayed with a different payload
stable_codes.EUM07: module_already_installed: a second install with a new key
stable_codes.40001: revision_conflict: the expected revision of a state command is stale
stable_codes.42501: house owner required; also direct edits of the command log or an out-of-sequence policy row
stable_codes.22023: invalid_policy_command: unknown module or state, bad key, missing or over-long reason, control characters
stable_codes.55P03: lock wait exceeded 5 s; nothing changed, the same key can be sent again
